weather_reasons: Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 140006
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
506 PM MST Sun Sep 13 2026

.UPDATE...00Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Abundant moisture will remain situated across the eastern half
  of Arizona providing enhanced chances for showers and 
  thunderstorms through the middle portion of the week, especially
  over the mountain locations.

- Although uncertainty remains, there will be potential for some 
  storms to produce strong gusty and heavy rainfall leading to 
  localized flash flooding over the next several days.

- Near to slightly above normal temperatures are expected
  throughout the upcoming week. 
 
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Monday/...
Latest objective analysis depicts the subtropical ridge of high 
pressure situated over Texas while a robust upper-trough is 
situated over the northwestern CONUS. The ridge of high pressure 
is forecast to reposition over the southeastern states while broad
troughing will remain situated to the northwest of the region 
through much of the upcoming week. This overall pattern 
configuration will continue to result in south to south-southwest 
flow over the area, aiding with periodic moisture influxes and 
thus an elevated potential of shower and thunderstorm activity,
mainly across central and eastern AZ.

The 12z KPHX sounding from early this morning depicted a very moist 
airmass in place with a low-level mixing ratio of 14 g/kg and PWATs 
in excess of 1.9". The abundant moisture already in place combined 
with strong daytime heating will result in MLCAPE values this 
afternoon between 1500-2000 J/KG across much of south-central AZ 
with near zero convective inhibition. Even though the thermodynamics 
look very favorable for thunderstorms, the main limiting factor 
for widespread coverage continues to be lack of good upper-level 
forcing for ascent given that most of the jet dynamics associated 
with the troughing pattern over the northwestern states will 
remain to the north of the region. Therefore, thunderstorm 
activity this afternoon through early this evening will be 
orographically induced, with the latest hi-res guidance showing 
isolated to widely scattered activity across the eastern and 
southeast third of AZ this afternoon. However, even though the hi-
res guidance shows little to no activity further west into Pinal 
and Maricopa Counties, given the lack of convective inhibition in 
place, it will not take much to get storms to pop up in the 
smaller terrain features such as the Table Top Mountains and the 
Estrellas, with potential outflows potentially instigating new 
storm development in the lower elevations, including into portions
of the Phoenix area. With these storms that do develop, given the
very moist environment in place, heavy rainfall leading to 
localized flash flooding will be the primary threat with a 
secondary threat being strong downburst wind gusts given that 
DCAPE values are expected to range between 1000-1200 J/KG. With 
the loss of daytime heating, storm activity should diminish by 
early this evening. 

Heading into the overnight and early morning hours on Monday, 
several of the hi-res guidance indicate a round of elevated 
showers and storms materializing across portions of south-central 
AZ, including the Phoenix area. This is likely due to a northern 
Sonora storm complex that is being depicted by guidance to develop
later this evening and is likely to send a gravity wave/outflow 
northward and aid as the triggering mechanism for convective 
development. Latest NBM is honing in on this potential, showing 
PoPs between 30-50% from central Phoenix eastward into Gila 
County. Heading into Monday afternoon, there is a greater signal 
for better storm coverage across southeast AZ with activity 
impacting the higher terrain areas east of Phoenix. However, given
that the convective inhibition will once again be nearly absent 
due to abundant moisture in place with low-level mixing ratios of 
12-14 g/kg and at least 1500 J/KG of MLCAPE assuming the morning 
activity does not disrupt the daytime heating significantly, a 
modest outflow is likely to be sufficient to trigger additional 
storm activity across the lower deserts of south-central AZ. 
Similar to today, heavy rainfall leading to localized flash 
flooding will be the primary threat. 

Temperatures during the next couple of days will be near to slightly 
above normal levels with afternoon highs ranging between 100-107 
degrees, with the warmest readings across the western deserts,
along with above normal early morning lows in the low to mid 80s.
This will maintain the overall HeatRisk level in the moderate 
category.

&&

.LONG TERM /Tuesday through Saturday/...
The weather pattern through at least the middle of the week will 
continue to support good moisture levels over at least the eastern 
half of Arizona and likely improved upper level ascent for Tuesday-
Thursday. Tuesday may involve a brief period of drier air moving 
into south-central Arizona from the southwest and this shows up in 
the fairly limited PoPs Tuesday afternoon/evening. However, NBM 
guidance shows a resurgence of moisture and rain chances during the 
overnight hours Tuesday night/Wednesday morning. Chances Wednesday 
into Thursday are also looking better with a potential disturbance 
tracking northward into central/eastern Arizona at some point. 
Needless to say, the model differences call into question the best 
timing for rain chances and the exact areas, but as long as the 
upper level support and good moisture remain present chances will 
remain elevated. 

WPC has added a slight risk on the Days 2-4 (Monday- Wednesday) 
Excessive Rainfall Outlooks over the eastern Arizona high terrain. 
It would not be surprising for subsequent issuance's of the EROs to 
extend the risk through Thursday or even Friday depending on the 
forecast available moisture. Although the risk for heavy rainfall 
and flooding will be present through at least the middle of the 
week, the risk for strong downdraft/outflow winds is likely to 
decrease with guidance showing decreasing forecast DCAPEs. Models 
are still trending toward drier air finally moving eastward through 
most of Arizona by Friday or Saturday. This should mostly shut down 
rain chances over the lower deserts and decrease chances over higher 
terrain areas.

Temperatures throughout the entire week are expected to remain 
fairly close to seasonal normals with the lowest forecast highs 
occurring on Tuesday and Wednesday. As long as models are correct 
with the drying trend late in the week into next weekend, 
temperatures are favored to drift back to above normal with highs 
more in a 103-108 degree range by Friday or Saturday.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0000Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
The main aviation concerns this forecast period will be the
potential for SHRA/TSRA developing over the Phoenix Metro early
Monday morning around sunrise. There is still a good amount of
uncertainty as to which terminals see any direct impacts.
Currently chances for TS are highest (20-30%) at KIWA and KPHX.
The main impacts from any storms that do develop will be gusty
S-SE winds and potential brief reductions in vsby due to heavy
rainfall. High-res guidance indicates the initial batch of
SHRA/TSRA clearing east of the TAF sites by 16Z-17Z. There could
also be a second round which develops by the late afternoon/early
evening, and a PROB30 group has been added to KPHX to reflect this
possibility. The wind forecast will not be a straight forward
tomorrow with most models showing southerly flow prevailing
through much of the day before returning out of the southeast by
the early evening. Clouds will remain few through this evening,
becoming SCT to BKN by early Monday morning with bases hovering 
around 8-9 kft.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No aviation weather concerns will exist through the TAF period
under mostly clear skies. Confidence is high that winds will
behave similar to the past 24 hours varying between southeasterly
and southwesterly at KIPL and southerly to southwesterly at KBLH 
with periods of calm and vrb conditions anticipated early Monday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Chances for scattered showers and isolated storms will continue 
today before increasing and becoming more widespread into the south-
central Arizona lower deserts beginning Monday. Moisture levels will 
remain high enough to support localized heavy rainfall with any 
storms. Minimum humidity levels over the next several days will only 
fall into a 15-25% range in western districts and 25-40% in eastern 
districts. This will follow fair to good overnight recovery of 40-
70%. Outside of thunderstorms, winds will generally remain light 
with a south to southwest heading though nearly calm conditions 
will be common in the morning hours. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Lojero
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...Salerno
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman
